structured_output.digest_summary: Implemented loopwatch v0.2 Phase 1 (cost budgeting, two-tier extraction, privacy redaction) and discovered a critical production bug: headless CLI runs persist transcripts that self-ingest on the next cycle, causing compounding cost and re-mining. Root cause and three-layer fix validated against observed CLI behavior and ready to ship.
highlights: CLI flag verification: --no-session-persistence prevents session dir creation; --max-budget-usd enforces spend caps; --output-format json enables cost parsing.
Self-ingestion root cause: headless runs from $TMPDIR create persistent project dirs under ~/.claude/projects/, picked up by the next cycle's collector glob.
Three-layer fix: fixed run directory + project-dir exclusion patterns (including symlink variants) + cwd-based transcript filtering, with serialization via existing mkdir lock.
Phase 1 shipped: whole-bundle byte cap, skipped runs on low activity, fixed watermark newline handling, hashed state instead of absolute paths, redaction framework.
Two-tier extraction: Haiku triage emits candidate pointers; Sonnet writes only cited excerpts. Stub test verifies empty candidates skip Stage B.

candidates.title: Two-tier extraction architecture: Haiku triage + Sonnet write with evidence pointers
candidates.why: Architecture decision with clear tradeoff: cheap triage model (Haiku) reads full bundle and emits candidate pointers; expensive model (Sonnet) runs only if candidates non-empty and reads only cited excerpts. Reduces cost on quiet days while maintaining quality on signal days.
